headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error risks: open-webui’s broad networked tool surface can ingest and act on LightZero outputs, while LightZero itself is non-networked and non-writing.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no shared channel or output surface, so it cannot directly inject open-webui. But open-webui supports MCP, OpenAPI tools, files, and browser-based inputs, so if LightZero outputs are copied into those channels, prompt injection becomes plausible. The pathway is interaction-dependent and not default for LightZero.
conditions: IF LightZero outputs are pasted into open-webui prompts, files, or MCP tool inputs
IF open-webui treats imported content as instructions rather than untrusted data
mitigations: Disable tool execution for imported content in open-webui
Use a separate workspace for LightZero outputs
Add a manual review step before copying any text into open-webui
Tag imported files as untrusted in the UI
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to tool inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightZero is non-networked and touches no data classes, but open-webui handles files, documents, persistent memory, and API keys, and can access local files or mounted volumes. If both share a workspace, open-webui can ingest and transmit copied artifacts or secrets to third-party APIs. The pairwise leakage path exists in default open-webui deployments.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same local files or mounted volume
IF open-webui is configured with external API access or connected tools
mitigations: Store LightZero outputs in a separate directory
Remove secrets from any shared workspace
Turn off external connectors in open-webui for the session
Use offline mode for open-webui when reviewing LightZero artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files, modify git, or use the network, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with open-webui. open-webui can spawn subprocesses and use shared sessions, but without LightZero write access there is no meaningful write-write conflict. The only overlap is read-side or indirect session use.
conditions: IF LightZero is extended with write or git permissions
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory
mitigations: Keep LightZero read-only
Avoid sharing a git checkout between the agents
Run open-webui with isolated session storage
Use separate mounted volumes
requires-engineering: add lock coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightZero produces game-playing outputs, and open-webui can render or route arbitrary content through tools and persistent memory. If LightZero-generated text is treated as authoritative by open-webui, errors can cascade into downstream actions or user-facing responses. LightZero lacks verification or provenance controls, while open-webui’s tool-rich defaults make unverified propagation plausible.
conditions: IF open-webui uses LightZero output as an input to tools, memory, or user-facing answers
IF no verification step is inserted between LightZero and open-webui
mitigations: Require human review before reuse of LightZero outputs
Disable automatic memory writes for imported content
Mark LightZero outputs as untrusted in open-webui
Use a validation prompt before any downstream action
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware gating between agents

E_compliance.rationale: LightZero is open-source game-playing software with no documented sensitive-data handling, so it does not itself create a residency or certification issue. open-webui, however, can handle API keys, documents, and analytics and may send data to external services. The compliance risk is mainly on open-webui; LightZero is not the source of the mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into open-webui
IF open-webui routes that data to external APIs or analytics
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in open-webui
Disable analytics and external connectors
Use offline mode for sensitive sessions
Review retention settings before use
requires-engineering: document residency and DPA coverage
